title: 1963 AHSME Problem 34
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) side \(a=\sqrt3,\) side \(b=\sqrt3,\) and side \(c\gt3.\) Let \(x\) be the largest number such that the magnitude, in degrees, of the angle opposite side \(c\) exceeds \(x.\) Then \(x\) equals:

solutions.text:
The law of cosines gives \[\cos C=\frac{3+3-c^2}{2\sqrt3\sqrt3}=\frac{6-c^2}{6}.\] Since \(c\gt3,\) \(\cos C\lt-\frac{1}{2},\) so \(C\gt120^\circ.\) Values can approach \(120^\circ\) as \(c\) approaches \(3\) from above, so the largest guaranteed bound is \(120.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Use the law of cosines for the angle \(C\) opposite \(c\)
